prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1405; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a left-turn collision at an intersection and stated a knee injury from the impact; the claim was opened and the file assigned for review.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and spoke with the other driver, who described the collision the same way the claimant did; the driver is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time.

Entry 3: Two independent witnesses and scene photographs match the described sequence, and the police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle when it happened.

Entry 4: Vehicle damage was inspected and is consistent with the reported impact; no prior damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 5: Claimant's account has stayed the same across every call and written statement, with no changes in the details of the turn or the impact.

Entry 6: Medical records show the knee injury fits the kind and force of the crash, and no earlier injury to that body area is known from the claimant's history or prior records.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a usual course and tapered as the claimant improved; the file is being prepared for the injury evaluation with no open questions on causation.
